{
  "project_id": "P-UK-HyNetCCUSCluster",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Incremental deployment of initial anchor projects leaves spare storage capacity, creating a risk of T&S network underutilisation and revenue support exposure.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Run the HyNet top-up process to recruit additional industrial emitters and fill remaining network storage capacity.",
      "evidence": "introduces a risk of network underutilisation and revenue support exposure, but represents the most effective way to deploy CCUS."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Executing T&S FID prior to anchor capture projects achieving FID creates financial exposure and schedule mismatch risks if capture projects fail to close.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Enforce strict financial and permitting conditions precedent on anchor projects prior to contract finalisation.",
      "evidence": "We plan to execute Eni’s FID (T&S FID) first with Protos and EETH taking their FIDs afterwards."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Low UK ETS carbon market prices fail to provide adequate private sector incentive to invest in carbon capture without long-term government subsidies.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide long-term CfD-style revenue support contracts to guarantee strike price coverage over key operational periods.",
      "evidence": "The Carbon Price is currently too low to incentivise deployment, there is a first-mover disadvantage due to high start-up costs"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Risk of CO2 leakage from deep offshore geological storage reservoirs in Liverpool Bay causing environmental harm and financial liabilities.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Underwrite key leakage liabilities via the Supplementary Compensation Agreement and install offshore sentinel and monitoring wells.",
      "evidence": "government will underwrite several key high-impact, low-probably risks – principally relating to CO2 leakage – via the Supplementary Compensation Agreement (SCA)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Capital expenditure overruns during Eni's construction of the onshore and offshore T&S network could inflate cluster deployment costs.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Apply a regulatory cost-sharing mechanism where the T&SCo recoups only 40% of expenditure exceeding the agreed regulatory capital baseline.",
      "evidence": "overruns against this allowance subject to a cost sharing factor; the T&SCo will only recoup 40% of any costs in excess of the agreed level."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Escalating costs of industrial emissions without available CCUS infrastructure could force energy-intensive manufacturers to relocate outside the UK.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Accelerate CCUS cluster deployment and industrial business model subsidies to safeguard domestic industrial competitiveness.",
      "evidence": "manufacturers of critical industrial materials may relocate to more favourable jurisdictions due to the escalating costs of emissions; otherwise known as ‘carbon leakage’."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Delays in final funding approval beyond time-limited supplier bids force developers to re-negotiate vendor contracts, driving up costs and causing schedule slippage.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Progress approvals ahead of the Spending Review or negotiate bid extensions directly with supply chain partners.",
      "evidence": "If the approval of the FFE is delayed we would need to postpone FID and developers would need to re-negotiate supplier bids."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Complex cross-chain interdependencies between the T&SCo and capture projects risk financial and operational disruption if network downtime or outages occur.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide targeted government underwriting for cross-chain risks and establish oversight via the DESNZ Cluster Sponsor Function.",
      "evidence": "learnings from the cancelled second CCUS competition in 2016 showed that private sector developers and insurers are not yet ready to bear the ‘cross-chain’ risks"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Dispersing post-FID contract management across DESNZ, Ofgem, LCCC, and CGL introduces governance coordination risks and operational friction.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish the DESNZ Cluster Sponsor Function to coordinate cross-body operations and execute defined Integrated Processes.",
      "evidence": "No single party is suitable to manage all of these agreements, and so contract management responsibilities are dispersed across multiple organisations."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Shortfalls in network demand or user fees trigger exchequer payout liabilities under the Revenue Support Agreement to cover T&S allowed revenues.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Regular monitoring by LCCC and DESNZ alongside top-up emitter onboarding to maintain adequate T&S network flow volumes.",
      "evidence": "If there was a shortfall in demand for the network, and aggregate user fees did not meet the T&SCos allowed revenue, government guarantees these fees"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Build-out projects (Padeswood and Viridor) failing or delaying taking FID results in prolonged T&S network underutilisation.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Agree Statements of Principles early and enforce delivery maturity requirements prior to individual build-out FBC approvals.",
      "evidence": "risk that if one or more of the build-out projects in HyNet fails to take FID, the network as a whole will be underutilised"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Partner ALBs and regulators may lack the staffing capacity and specialized capability required for effective post-FID administration.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Require Organisational Readiness Statements and run pre-FID checkpoints to identify and resolve resource or skill gaps.",
      "evidence": "To assess capacity and capability of key partner organisations to deliver their roles at FID, the CCUS programme commissioned partner organisations... Organisational Readiness Statements."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Constraints in supply chain capacity and specialized vendor availability drive up equipment procurement costs and delay delivery dates.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Leverage external technical advisors, manage procurement schedules incrementally, and engage key vendors early.",
      "evidence": "Given the limited supplier market capability, and loss of confidence in the UK CCUS vision, underlying costs are expected to increase."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Incremental deployment of initial anchor projects leaves spare storage capacity, creating a risk of T&S network underutilisation and revenue support exposure.
risks.mitigation: Run the HyNet top-up process to recruit additional industrial emitters and fill remaining network storage capacity.
risks.evidence: introduces a risk of network underutilisation and revenue support exposure, but represents the most effective way to deploy CCUS.

risks.description: Executing T&S FID prior to anchor capture projects achieving FID creates financial exposure and schedule mismatch risks if capture projects fail to close.
risks.mitigation: Enforce strict financial and permitting conditions precedent on anchor projects prior to contract finalisation.
risks.evidence: We plan to execute Eni’s FID (T&S FID) first with Protos and EETH taking their FIDs afterwards.

risks.description: Low UK ETS carbon market prices fail to provide adequate private sector incentive to invest in carbon capture without long-term government subsidies.
risks.mitigation: Provide long-term CfD-style revenue support contracts to guarantee strike price coverage over key operational periods.

risks.mitigation: Underwrite key leakage liabilities via the Supplementary Compensation Agreement and install offshore sentinel and monitoring wells.
risks.evidence: government will underwrite several key high-impact, low-probably risks – principally relating to CO2 leakage – via the Supplementary Compensation Agreement (SCA).

risks.evidence: overruns against this allowance subject to a cost sharing factor; the T&SCo will only recoup 40% of any costs in excess of the agreed level.

risks.mitigation: Require Organisational Readiness Statements and run pre-FID checkpoints to identify and resolve resource or skill gaps.
